newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ING Barings no comment on compensation.
newsitem.headline: ING Barings no comment on compensation.

text.p: ING Groep NV unit ING Barings said it had no comment on a newspaper report that bondholders who lost 275 million stg ($444 million) in the collapse of the Barings merchant bank could receive compensation payments in coming months.
The Times of London said ING Barings and other unnamed parties were looking for a suitable mechanism to make the payments, adding that negotiations were at a delicate stage.
But a spokesman for ING Barings told Reuters: "There's nothing to say specifically about the bondholders."
ING bought Barings for 1.7 billion guilders ($900 million) in March 1995 after the merchant bank collapsed from trading losses.
Since then the Barings operations have been absorbed into the ING Barings investment banking unit.
Investors in the bonds began legal action in January against a number of parties involved in the various bond issues and former Barings executives.

The Times said if the payments were contested, they could be delayed. It listed three categories of investors - those holding $150 million of notes issued in 1986, holders of $150 million of notes issued in 1994 and holders of 100 million stg of perpetual notes issued in 1994.
